name: The Beaubien household — a name the town's own records carry

division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the west division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's tradesman_dwellings clause. The frame cottages fall on the side streets behind the principal frontages — the back of the same blocks the stores front, which is how a block parcel comes to deal its meanest roof to its worst street. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO DATED EVIDENCE AT OR BEFORE 1835-07-01. present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

married.what_happened: NOT DRAWN FOR THIS HOUSE: MOVED INTO IT. The household model drew this house married and the order book had no woman left in its wife's cell, so no wife was drawn. Josette Pelletier headed a house of her own, dealt by T-1174 to fill the women and children the age pyramid lacked; she fits this house by its own rules — her division, a band never above his, no child older than his band allows — and T-2020 folds her house into his: she is his wife here and the 5 of her house come with her. Every name, age band and seed is the one T-1174 drew; the children keep the surname they were dealt with. Both people are the town's invention at the `reconstructed` tier, and the marriage is too: no source says B Beaubien married anybody.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('beaubien_b:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.
